bug_semantics: An authenticated user could persist an arbitrary ConnectURL through the JWT-protected add-Connect operation. The server-side GetConnectsInfo path then read every stored URL and called the unrestricted HTTP helper on TrimURL(conn.ConnectURL) + "/api/connect"; the route introduced with that behavior was public, and later peer-info/health paths reused the same unsafe fetch. With no scheme/host/IP validation and no DNS-safe dialer, a stored peer URL could drive server-originated requests to loopback, private networks, link-local cloud metadata, or internal DNS names.
flaw_origin: fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 is the smallest real origin: it added GetConnectsInfo, the public GET /api/connects/info route, and pkg.SendRequest, moving peer-detail retrieval from browser-side direct requests to an unvalidated server-side request. Later commits only modified, moved, or extracted that already-vulnerable operation; in particular d87ddc2085435189b969cffbdc5f87640e6e7929 rewrote/moved the existing v1 implementation into the 2.x tree and 2d1698c515ebdd3945c30b22f17e517893a4be9a extracted it into fetchPeerConnectInfo.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-8mc6-xjpr-h98x names fetchPeerConnectInfo's use of SendRequest instead of SendSafeRequest, gives private/cloud-metadata targets, and declares 4.7.3 patched; the assigned downstream advisory maps this mechanism to CVE-2026-79659/GHSA-9G26-825H-8V6P and Ech0 before 4.7.3.

In the clone, `git show --format=fuller --find-renames fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3` shows one focused feature commit adding: internal/services/connect_service.go GetConnectsInfo, which iterates repository.GetAllConnects and invokes pkg.SendRequest(pkg.TrimURL(conn.ConnectURL)+"/api/connect", "GET"); pkg/other.go SendRequest backed by http.Client.Do with no validation; and publicRoutes.GET("/connects/info", controllers.GetConnectsInfo). The same diff shows the web store changing from browser-side per-peer fetchGetConnect calls to this server endpoint, establishing the causal server-side-fetch transition.

Direct-parent verification: `git show 4e343d6638b14e535a8fda2c258724527ff533e4:internal/services/connect_service.go`, `:internal/routers/routers.go`, and `:pkg/other.go` shows AddConnect/GetConnects but no GetConnectsInfo, no /connects/info route, and no SendRequest helper. The parent is the v1.2.8 tag target. Thus the complete server-side SSRF mechanism is absent immediately before the BIC.

Lineage verification: `git log 397fc6fc46cceaa02a745cc51d8e58b78a8edcc2 -L :GetConnectsInfo:Ech0_OLD/internal/services/connect_service.go --format=fuller --patch` terminates at fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3. It also shows subsequent concurrency/retry changes preserving the same stored ConnectURL -> pkg.SendRequest operation. `git log 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc^ -L :fetchPeerConnectInfo:internal/service/connect/connect.go` points to extraction commit 2d1698c515ebdd3945c30b22f17e517893a4be9a, while inspection of that commit and its earlier tree shows it merely extracted the pre-existing unsafe request rather than introducing it.

BIC commit-object-only AI check: `git cat-file -p fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3` prints author and committer `L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com>` and only the message `feat: 添加获取 Connect 信息的功能，并更新相关路由和常量`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker. AI attribution on the later fix commit is deliberately excluded by the protocol.

Closing fix: `git show --format=fuller 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc -- internal/service/connect/connect.go` changes fetchPeerConnectInfo from SendRequest to SendSafeRequest and adds ValidatePublicHTTPURL at AddConnect. At its parent cecc2c19b590df85d79ea98457faa143130cd620, internal/util/http/http.go shows SendSafeRequest validating http/https URLs, blocking local/private/reserved targets, using SecureDialContext after DNS resolution, and revalidating redirects; therefore 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc directly closes both stored-URL insertion and request-time egress paths.

Release boundary: `git describe --contains --match='v*' --tags fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3` returns v1.2.9~2, while the BIC parent is v1.2.8, making v1.2.9 the first tagged vulnerable release in Git history. `git describe --contains --match='v*' --tags 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc` returns v4.7.3~5. `git tag --contains 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc` includes v4.7.3 and later but not v4.7.2, and `git diff v4.7.2..v4.7.3 -- internal/service/connect/connect.go internal/util/http/http.go` displays the unsafe-to-safe request change and insertion-time validation. Thus tagged vulnerable releases run from v1.2.9 through v4.7.2, with v4.7.3 the first patched release.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 turns a previously client-side peer lookup into a server-side public aggregation endpoint and supplies an unrestricted HTTP helper for attacker-influenced stored URLs. The immediate parent has storage operations but none of the server-side egress mechanism, satisfying direct parent absence. History across the 2.x rewrite and the later fetchPeerConnectInfo extraction preserves the same vulnerable operation, so neither later commit is the BIC. Commit 091d26d2d942df6df9f520328d2f9cf2592bbefc directly switches runtime fetching to the existing SSRF-safe helper and adds defense-in-depth validation before persistence; tag ancestry places that fix first in 4.7.3. The BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI disclosure or bot marker. Under BIC-only attribution, the later fix's Claude co-author trailer cannot support an AI-origin verdict, so the closed result is NOT_AI.
